title: Derived exchange on lifted closed pro-etale test objects
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and put $\Lambda_Y=p_Y^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use internal module objects, exact module inverse images, and ordinary unbounded derived direct images computed on K-injectives [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, lem-zl-condensed-lisse-proetale-locality]. Let $f:X\to U$ be any morphism of affine schemes, $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and let $s:Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)\hookrightarrow U$ be a closed immersion. Write $X_Z=X\times_U Z$ with maps $h:X_Z\to X$, $f_Z:X_Z\to Z$. On the affine ind-etale bases let $v$ be the closed-site lift [def-exc-closed-site-lift]. Let $V\to Z$ be an affine ind-etale object, and suppose both $V$ and $v(V)$ are w-contractible affine schemes [sk-def-pe-wlocal]. Put $T=X\times_Uv(V)$ and $T_0=X\times_UV$, with induced closed immersion $a:T_0\hookrightarrow T$, and let $K$ be any bounded-below object of $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_X})$.
There are canonical natural isomorphisms in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$
$$R\Gamma(V,s^*Rf_*K)\cong R\Gamma(T,K|_T),\qquad R\Gamma(V,R(f_Z)_*h^*K)\cong R\Gamma(T_0,K|_{T_0}).$$
Under these isomorphisms the derived exchange, defined as the $f_Z^*\dashv R(f_Z)_*$-adjunct of $f_Z^*s^*Rf_*K\cong h^*f^*Rf_*K\xrightarrow{h^*\varepsilon}h^*K$, is exactly the canonical derived restriction
$$R\Gamma(T,K|_T)\longrightarrow R\Gamma(T_0,a^*(K|_T)).$$
Canonical restriction means the derived adjunction unit for $a$ followed by the composition comparison for derived direct images. These identifications are natural in $K$, in maps of admissible test objects, in isomorphisms of the square, and under pro-etale base change of $U$, using the site localizations and canonical composition comparisons. No assertion that the displayed restriction or exchange is invertible is included.
For a morphism of condensed rings $\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ and a module map $K\to\operatorname{Res}N$ (where $N$ is bounded below over $\Lambda'_X$), the displayed comparison squares commute with the derived maps induced by that actual module map after restriction of scalars. Here the direct-image coefficient comparison is the right-derived comparison induced by the sectionwise identity $f_*\operatorname{Res}=\operatorname{Res}f_*$; it need not be invertible. In particular this applies to the ordinary scalar-extension unit $M\to\operatorname{Res}(\Lambda'_X\otimes_{\Lambda_X}M)$, $x\mapsto1\otimes x$, for a degree-zero module $M$.

proof.text: Pass between internal modules and ordinary modules over the reconstructed section-ring sheaf using the equivalence, which is the identity on underlying abelian sheaves, sections and restriction maps. An equivalence of abelian categories is exact and preserves the defining null-homotopy criterion for K-injectivity. Thus the following calculations in section-ring modules calculate the required internal-module functors, rather than a different coefficient theory. Every module inverse image in the square is exact with underlying sheaf the ordinary inverse image: by definition $b^*M=\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_b}(b^*_{\Ab}M)$, the coefficient map $\alpha_b$ is an isomorphism of ring objects, so $\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_b}\cong\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha_b^{-1}}$ is the identity on underlying sheaves, and inverse image of abelian sheaves is exact. The locality lemma records the same coefficient identification on derived categories. Direct images have underlying section formula $(b_*F)(W)=F(X\times_YW)$ with action through the coefficient unit.

source.place: Tags 09BK–09BL, with the specified internal-module/section-ring equivalence and coefficient identifications

proof.text: The closed-site lift satisfies $V=v(V)\times_UZ$, so $T_0=T\times_{v(V)}V$, and every point of $v(V)$ specializes to a point of $V$. Both $V$ and $v(V)$ are geometrically w-contractible by hypothesis; the source-affine evaluation theorem makes them weakly contractible in their ambient pro-etale sites, in the section universe, and since restriction to the affine ind-etale basis is an equivalence of sheaf categories (it determines sheaves and morphisms uniquely), epimorphisms correspond and the same holds in the basis sites. Put $B=\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(v(V))$, the identity object of its own affine ind-etale basis; the same two theorems (with $T=W=B$) make evaluation at $B$ surjective on epimorphisms of set sheaves there. Apply the closed-site counit theorem to $B$ and the ideal cutting out $V=B\times_UZ$, using the specialization property just recalled: its counit is invertible. The unit comparison theorem then says that the actual inverse-image unit section map $F(v(V))\to(s^{-1}F)(V)$, $y\mapsto s^{-1}y$, is a natural isomorphism of abelian groups for every abelian sheaf $F$ on $U$; this agrees with the closed evaluation formula $(s^{-1}F)(V)\cong F(v(V))$. Throughout, the identification $(s^*F)(V)\cong F(v(V))$ means this unit-section isomorphism. For a module sheaf it is $\Lambda_U(v(V))$-linear, being the evaluation of the module adjunction unit, whose underlying map is the abelian unit by step 1. The module evaluation theorem makes evaluation at $V$ and at $v(V)$ exact (it preserves homology).

source.place: Tags 09BK and 09BL (1)–(2); weakly contractible evaluation as used in the proof of (2)

proof.text:
Choose a K-injective representative $I$ of $K$. Since $f^*$ is exact and left adjoint to $f_*$, the right-adjoint preservation theorem says that $f_*I$ is K-injective. Hence $Rf_*K$ is represented by $f_*I$. Evaluation at $V$ is exact by step 2, and $s^*$ is exact by step 1, so
$$R\Gamma(V,s^*Rf_*K)=Q\bigl((s^*f_*I)(V)\bigr)=Q\bigl(I(T)\bigr).$$
Here $Q$ means passage from a complex of abelian groups to $D(\mathbf{Ab})$; both equalities denote the canonical natural isomorphisms, not choices of unrelated identifications. The final equality is the inverse of the unit-section isomorphism of step 2, followed by the direct-image section formula $(f_*I)(v(V))=I(T)$. Derived section localization identifies $Q(I(T))$ with $R\Gamma(T,K|_T)$: on the localized site the comparison is the degreewise identity. This constructs the first displayed isomorphism.

Choose a K-injective resolution $j:h^*I\to J$. Exactness of $h^*$ makes $J$ a representative of $h^*K$. The same exact-left-adjoint argument as in step 3 makes $(f_Z)_*J$ K-injective. Exact evaluation at $V$ and the direct-image section formula give
$$R\Gamma(V,R(f_Z)_*h^*K)=Q\bigl(J(T_0)\bigr).$$
Derived section localization identifies this with $R\Gamma(T_0,(h^*K)|_{T_0})$. Here $T_0=h^{-1}(T)=X_Z\times_XT$, and $a$ is the localized morphism $h_T$ of the sites over $T_0$ and $T$. The localization square of ringed sites gives the canonical identification $(h^*K)|_{T_0}=j_{T_0}^*h^*K\cong(h_T)^*j_T^*K=a^*(K|_T)$, compatible with the coefficient identifications; with exact pullbacks it is applied termwise. We have therefore obtained the second displayed isomorphism with the coefficients and the target object specified in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0D6F; derived.tex Tag 08BJ; canonical pullback composition on modules

proof.text: Compute the ordinary mate on a module $F$, before deriving. By step 2 every element of $(s^*f_*F)(V)$ is the unit section $s^{-1}x$ of a unique $x\in(f_*F)(v(V))=F(T)$; the unit for $f_Z$ sends this to the corresponding inverse-image section on $T_0$. Under $f_Z^*s^*\cong h^*f^*$ the same section is represented by $x$ on the test object $v(V)$ and the map $T_0\to T=X\times_Uv(V)$. The counit $f^*f_*F\to F$ sends the representative indexed by $W\to U$ to its evaluation on $X\times_UW$; this is the defining Kan-extension/adjunction counit. At $W=v(V)$ the unit followed by this counit cancels by the triangle identity. The resulting section of $h^*F$ on $T_0$ is precisely the inverse-image unit section of $x\in F(T)$ for $a:T_0\to T$. Thus evaluation of the ordinary mate is the canonical restriction $F(T)\to(a^*F|_T)(T_0)$. This calculation uses neither invertibility of this map nor exactness of a closed direct image.

source.place: Tag 09BL (1)–(2), followed by the unit–counit calculation for the mate specified in the item

proof.text:
Apply step 5 degreewise to $I$, then apply $(f_Z)_*(j)$. This gives a chain map
$$e:s^*f_*I\longrightarrow(f_Z)_*J.$$
It represents the specified derived exchange: the derived-adjunction normalization identifies the derived counit on $I$ with its underived counit followed by the resolution comparison; transposing under $f_Z^*\dashv R(f_Z)_*$ therefore gives exactly $Q(e)$. Equivalently its transpose is $h^*\varepsilon_f$ followed by $j$, with the stated pullback comparison inserted, which characterizes the exchange uniquely. Since evaluation at $V$ is exact, its evaluated map is $Q(e(V))$. Step 5 computes this as the complex map
$$I(T)\longrightarrow(h^*I)(T_0)\xrightarrow{j(T_0)}J(T_0).$$
The first arrow is the unit section of $a$ after localization; the second is the chosen target resolution comparison.

source.place: Tags 0FND, 0DVC and 09T5, derived adjunction and its normalization by the ordinary counit; proetale.tex Tag 09BL

proof.text: Under the two section-localization identifications, the complex map at the end of step 6 is the derived restriction in the statement. Indeed the unit for $a^*\dashv Ra_*$, followed by the derived composition comparison for sections and $a_*$, is computed by the ordinary unit followed by a K-injective resolution of the pulled-back complex. This is exactly the map just displayed. For the section composition apply the K-injective composition theorem with $F=a_*$ and $G=\Gamma(T,-)$: $a_*$ preserves K-injectives because $a^*$ is exact. On a K-injective target resolution its comparison is the degreewise identity $\Gamma(T,a_*J)=\Gamma(T_0,J)$; the universal right-derived unit fixes this normalization. Only compositions of geometric direct images use the exact-left-adjoint composition/adjunction normalization theorem. Localization of the ringed-site adjunction preserves its unit and counit. Thus the equality is an equality in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$ of the canonical arrows with the normalizations requested in the statement.

source.place: Tags 0D6E–0D6F, derived pushforward composition and localized sections; derived.tex Tag 09T5

proof.text: The identifications do not depend on the resolutions. For a morphism $K\to K'$, the K-injective Hom theorem represents it by a unique homotopy class $I\to I'$. The unit-section isomorphism of step 2, restriction, and both chain-unit constructions commute with this chain map, by naturality of adjunction units. A homotopy remains a homotopy after applying every additive functor used here, so their equality descends to the derived categories. Changes of K-injective representative are homotopy equivalences with these same transition maps. This proves naturality in $K$ and independence of $I,J$. For a map of admissible test objects, use the naturality in $V$ of the unit-section isomorphism of step 2, and the ordinary presheaf restriction maps on $I(T)$ and $J(T_0)$; the unit-section square commutes by naturality of the unit. These calculations prove the test-object naturality as well.

proof.text: An isomorphism of the geometric square identifies the fiber products, the coefficient inverse images, and their units and counits. It therefore identifies each of the maps in steps 3–7. For pro-etale base change of $U$, interpret restriction through the corresponding site localization. The localized direct-image comparison has the section formula $(f_*F)(W)=F(X\times_UW)$, and the derived localized comparison commutes with units and counits. Pullback composition identifies the two restrictions of $K$ on each further fiber product. Thus localizing the unit-section map of step 5 gives the unit-section map for the base-changed square. Applying the canonical derived composition comparisons from step 7 proves the asserted compatibility for every base-changed admissible test, without replacing any noninvertible closed exchange by an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, canonical derived composition; ringed-site localization comparison and its unit/counit compatibility

proof.text: For $\Lambda\to\Lambda'$, restriction of scalars is exact and is the identity on underlying section groups. Its ordinary direct-image square $f_*\operatorname{Res}=\operatorname{Res}f_*$ is consequently the sectionwise identity, and it commutes with inverse images after the pulled-back coefficient identifications. Derive this square using the right-derived universal transformation: precompose a proposed comparison with the universal unit, where it is the ordinary identity square. The bijection in the universal property then makes the comparison unique. Pasting this construction with evaluation and localization gives the same comparison, since before derivation both pastings are the identity on the same sections. In particular each of the ordinary unit-section squares in step 5 commutes with a module map and with scalar restriction. Deriving those commutative squares by the same universal property proves the coefficient squares for the derived isomorphisms and the exchange. Applying them to the given actual morphism $K\to\operatorname{Res}N$ proves the requested clause. No step asserts that $\operatorname{Res}$ takes K-injectives to K-injectives or that its direct-image comparison is invertible.

source.place: Right-derived universal comparison and its uniqueness; ordinary scalar restriction and normalized module adjunctions

proof.text: For a degree-zero module $M$, take $N=\Lambda'_X\otimes_{\Lambda_X}M$ in degree zero. The ordinary extension/restriction adjunction unit is the actual module morphism $m\mapsto1\otimes m$. It is therefore a permitted input to step 10, which gives the final assertion. This application uses the ordinary tensor product and imposes no flatness assumption on $\Lambda'$ over $\Lambda$. The zero module, empty affine test, identity closed immersion, and zero coefficient ring are covered by the same unit formulas; for the identity closed immersion the restriction and the normalized exchange are identities.
